races.name: 100% Racingtv Profits Back To Racing Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Flightofthephoenix
runners_data.note: Has won twice in his last five starts with back-to-back victories, trainer Charles Hills in good form (T14:3/21), and holds the perfect prominent style to track the hot pace before striking late; soft going is within range based on recent form, making this a strong profile fit.

runners_data.name: I'd Go Maniac
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who landed a win on good ground at Goodwood recently and is placed in 15 soft-going starts — runs prominently for Alan King who sends him here fresh off a 31-day break wearing headgear; prominent style suits the pace scenario ideally.

runners_data.name: Ribble River
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Lizzie Quinlan who has been freshened for 47 days and has decent soft-going course experience, though recent runs over longer trips on good ground show modest form; needs the pace truly to collapse to deliver a meaningful late challenge.

runners_data.name: Austrian Theory
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up racer arrives on a 17-day turnaround after a modest run, and five recent starts are all on good or similar ground with no wins in that sample — soft may suit in theory via headgear, but this profile needs the race to fall apart in front.

runners_data.name: Roland Garros
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner fitted with a tongue-tie who is not a natural soft-ground performer based on stamina tests over longer trips, but OR=66 gives weight relief and Cian Murphy (5) can press forward from the off — will set the pace but may not see out 1m3½f in soft conditions.

runners_data.name: Alpine Sierra
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old front-runner for Jim Goldie who won twice recently on good ground but has yet to win on soft in the recent five-run sample; will contest the lead enthusiastically but the going and extra stamina demand on this track may expose her limitations late.

runners_data.name: Revelio
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's 4-year-old hold-up type has only one soft-going run in recent history (a 10th on soft over 8f) and steps up sharply in trip from recent starts — the form over 10-12f on good is moderate and the combination of soft and inexperience at this trip is a concern.

runners_data.name: Spirit Catcher
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's hold-up horse runs just three days after its last start and has a competent soft-ground record in the past five runs; not flashy in recent form but consistent in soft conditions and at longer distances, giving it a quiet each-way profile.

runners_data.name: Recobella
runners_data.note: Arrives with genuine in-form claims — three wins in recent starts and a soft-going placed run — but as a true hold-up horse she has been redistributed to midfield because of the crowded rear of the field, meaning she will likely race closer to the pace than ideal and her full finishing kick may be compromised.

runners_data.name: Star Start
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Ruth Carr who has hit the frame in five of her last six starts and won recently on good ground; will contest the lead alongside Roland Garros and Alpine Sierra, meaning her energy reserves in soft ground over 1m3½f are likely to be drained by the multi-way early battle.

runners_data.name: Shahbaz
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's hold-up horse with a tongue-tie has run six times over 12f on good recently without a win, and in this race his natural racing style cannot be accommodated — pushed into a midfield berth, his closing punch will be blunted and the soft ground does not improve his profile given limited recent form in those conditions.

runners_data.name: Cavalry Call
runners_data.note: Patrick Morris's hold-up runner arrives on a 28-day break with a grim recent record — four finishes of 7th or worse — and, like Shahbaz, cannot slot into his preferred rear position given the number of genuine hold-up types in this field; recent soft-ground runs have brought modest efforts and the form reads too low to overcome the tactical disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Red Derek
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent racer for Lisa Williamson who has been absent 81 days and has placed in multiple soft-ground starts, though five finishes in the soft-going sample show a horse who runs his race without threatening to win — the long layoff and modest OR=52 mean he is likely to fill a mid-division role once more.

races.paceDynamic: Roland Garros, Alpine Sierra, and Star Start are all confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead on soft ground over 1m3½f at Haydock, virtually guaranteeing a strong, honest gallop from the outset. With three genuine pace horses fighting for the same real estate, the tempo will be pressured and relentless, placing a premium on stamina and the ability to sustain effort deep into the race on this testing surface. Prominent types sitting just off the pace — Flightofthephoenix and I'd Go Maniac — are ideally positioned to inherit momentum without burning early energy, while true hold-up horses face an additional complication: Recobella, Shahbaz, and Cavalry Call are genuine off-the-pace raiders who cannot all get to the rear as is their nature, meaning at least some will race in unnatural positions and are consequently less effective. The race shape strongly favours a prominent racer who can track the contested lead from a stalking position and hit the front in the straight with petrol still in the tank, as a true hold-up finish requires a meaningful gap to close that a fast-run soft-ground staying race may simply not deliver.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out by halfway, gifting the race to a prominent but patient tracker.
scenarios.body: Roland Garros, Alpine Sierra, and Star Start will cut each other up through a fierce first mile, leaving the strong-finishing prominent types Flightofthephoenix and I'd Go Maniac to sweep past the weakening pace-setters in the final two furlongs on soft ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pace Horse Escapes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners breaks cleanly and controls the pace without being forced into a truly excessive gallop.
scenarios.body: Should Roland Garros or Alpine Sierra find a clear rail position and dictate without being constantly pressured, they could build an unassailable lead by the straight before rivals realise the danger — soft ground rewards those who conserve energy by dominating rather than contesting.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Best
scenarios.trigger: If the pace truly collapses the entire field and leaves a gap for a late finisher to run through.
scenarios.body: Recobella has the best recent form among the hold-up types with multiple wins at this sort of trip, and if the front-runners have ruined each other completely, she could finish with a powerful run — however, her redistribution to midfield because of the crowded hold-up map means she is unlikely to get a fully clean passage late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Stamina Grind
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground deteriorates further and a fitness-based stamina grind eliminates all but the most durable stayers.
scenarios.body: A plodding, attritional finish suits a horse with proven soft-ground stamina and consistent recent form, giving Star Start and Ribble River a chance if rivals physically empty in the taxing conditions — but this scenario depends on ground and a pace collapse that leaves little difference in finishing positions.

watchPoints.text: Roland Garros, Alpine Sierra, and Star Start are all intent on the lead — watch the first two furlongs closely for a pace duel that could leave all three significantly weakened before halfway, which is the primary trigger for Scenario A.

Recobella's redistribution from hold-up to midfield is a material factor — if she is further forward than her natural style allows, she risks using energy she would normally conserve and her strong recent form may not translate into a winning performance.

Alpine Sierra has no recent soft-ground win in her last five starts — if ground conditions have worsened beyond routine soft, she may capitulate quickly after contesting the lead, and that is worth monitoring in the going report at race time.

Flightofthephoenix runs just six days after his last win, is trained by a yard firing at 3/21 in the 14-day window, and slots into the perfect prominent style for this shape — connections' confidence will be reflected in the market and any shortening from expected price is significant.

Spirit Catcher and Ribble River both have legitimate soft-going profiles and hold-up styles; if neither can get to the rear naturally because of the redistribution crunch, watch for one to be crowded or forced wider than ideal, which could cost them ground at a crucial point in the straight.

races.name: Jackie Harbridge In Loving Memory Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
Bailey Partnership Celebrating 50 Years Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tribal Appearance
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Dr Newland and Insole who returns after a 90-day absence; two soft-ground runs produced no wins or places from similar going, and the layoff combined with her deepest hold-up style makes the controlled pace here a genuine concern.

runners_data.name: Koodini
runners_data.note: Won over seven furlongs on Good for Hugo Palmer and David Probert and arrives here on a 14-day turnaround in decent form; two of her seven similar-going starts have produced a place, and she is the most credible of the genuine hold-up horses if pace develops.

runners_data.name: Vinery
runners_data.note: Third start for Greenall and Guerriero, showed a placed run over six furlongs at Goodwood on Good; moving up to seven furlongs on soft is uncharted territory and Charles Bishop will need to slot her smartly off the pace to get a proper run.

runners_data.name: High Hazard
runners_data.note: Palmer's second string alongside Koodini, but the flagged fading tendency is a real concern on soft ground over seven furlongs; has placed twice over eight furlongs on Good but soft-going form — 13th and 16th — is poor and she is vulnerable late.

runners_data.name: Katie's Cavalier
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and sole pace reference in this race; her STYLE_FIT tag notes she is racing somewhat out of role in a competitive nursery, but her uncontested lead on soft ground is a genuine tactical weapon and her Goodwood win over 7f is the most relevant recent form.

runners_data.name: Gerry's Darling
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's filly has placed form on Good over seven furlongs and arrives after a 27-day break in fair shape; as a naturally prominent racer she is ideally placed to track the leader and her consistent handicap form makes her one of the key pace beneficiaries.

runners_data.name: Green Titan
runners_data.note: George Boughey's four-time runner has placed on soft-ish ground twice from four starts and comes here on a 17-day turnaround with Pat Cosgrave aboard; a prominent style that has delivered placed runs on cut in the ground suits this soft-going 7f shape.

runners_data.name: Diplomata
runners_data.note: William Haggas and Tom Marquand hold a strong hand on paper, but this horse's true nature is as a hold-up type — pushed toward midfield on the map because the rear is congested — and Haggas's yard is in strong 14-day form (9/49); the repositioning means its best form may be harder to access here.

runners_data.name: Peggy's Lad
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's winner over seven furlongs at Southwell (all-weather) brings a prominent style and David Allan partnership; soft turf is a new test and his going profile is mainly Good or faster, so the underfoot conditions represent a mild unknown.

runners_data.name: Greek Street
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's hold-up type has placed over six furlongs on Standard and will be carried into midfield rather than his natural rear position; with limited soft-ground experience and a style that is compromised by the race shape, Sean Levey faces a tactical puzzle.

runners_data.name: One Shot Kodi
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's three-race maiden who steps up from six to seven furlongs on soft ground; the 14-day turnaround and a prominent style mean Tom Eaves can at least secure a useful position, but the form figures over six furlongs on Standard and Good leave the soft-going step up unproven.

runners_data.name: Unbeatable Fame
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's soft-ground regular — best form is a third at Goodwood on Good — arrives as a true hold-up runner who will find the redistribution to midfield a tactical headache; Fahey's strong 14-day strike rate (6/49) keeps her in the picture but the race shape does not play to her strengths.

races.paceDynamic: Katie's Cavalier is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner nursery and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, she is set to dictate from the gates at a measured, sustainable tempo over seven furlongs on Soft ground. Gerry's Darling, Green Titan, Peggy's Lad, and One Shot Kodi will press forward into prominent positions behind her, creating a bunched early-to-mid-race group that pushes along at a workmanlike pace rather than a true gallop. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Diplomata, Greek Street, and Unbeatable Fame are genuine closers who are each tagged redistributed and will struggle to find their natural position, likely settling closer to midfield than they would prefer. On soft ground over seven furlongs with a controlled, single-pacemaker tempo, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel economically in the slipstream of Katie's Cavalier and have the class to kick on from two furlongs out — hold-up horses dependent on a strong pace to fuel a late run are tactically disadvantaged here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cavalier Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Katie's Cavalier secures an uncontested lead and the pace remains honest but not punishing, the race is run to suit those positioned just behind her.
scenarios.body: Katie's Cavalier sets a comfortable rhythm on the soft, and the prominent runners tracking her — particularly Gerry's Darling, Green Titan, and Peggy's Lad — race within themselves before pouncing from two furlongs out; soft ground rewards those who conserve energy in the early stages and produce a sustained, grinding finish rather than a sharp burst.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Galvanise
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group goes quicker than expected in the soft and ties itself up, creating a genuine pace collapse in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Koodini and Tribal Appearance, operating from hold-up positions, would be best placed to pick up the pieces if the leaders hit the wall on testing ground; however, this scenario is tempered because several mapped midfield runners — Diplomata, Greek Street, Unbeatable Fame — are redistributed true hold-ups unlikely to be far enough back to produce a classical late surge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Front Runner Lasts
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group dawdles in the early stages and Katie's Cavalier, with no pressure, slips the field on good terms and is never truly challenged.
scenarios.body: Katie's Cavalier, solo and uncontested, saves enough energy on the soft to hold on as rivals find her already four or five lengths clear by the time they wind up; her recent win at Goodwood over this trip shows she can deliver on a sound surface, and soft ground may blunt the closers' ability to reel her in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Ground Chaos, Rank Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground causes widespread trouble in running, forcing pace horses wide and opening a gap for a lightly raced improver to emerge.
scenarios.body: Vinery — placed second over six furlongs on Good — is unexposed at seven furlongs and could improve significantly for the step up; High Hazard, despite a fading tendency, has placed on heavy-related ground and could outrun expectations if rivals fail to fire.

watchPoints.text: Katie's Cavalier holds a potentially race-defining uncontested lead — if Hector Crouch controls the fractions from the front on soft ground, rivals tracking prominently such as Gerry's Darling and Green Titan must time their challenges perfectly or risk being left flat-footed.

Diplomata, Greek Street, and Unbeatable Fame are all true hold-up runners mapped into midfield — watch whether Marquand, Levey, and McSweeney attempt to drop them back to their natural position at the cost of ground, or accept the compromised spot and hope pace materialises.

High Hazard carries a flagged fading tendency in a field where soft ground over seven furlongs will specifically expose that weakness in the closing stages — Sam James will need to manage the run carefully to avoid a repeat of her 13th and 16th on soft.

Koodini arrives on a 14-day turnaround and is the hold-up horse with the strongest soft-going placed form — David Probert's positioning in the first half-mile will be telling; if she is buried wide or too far back, her chance may evaporate before the straight.

The Hugo Palmer yard sends out two runners (Koodini and High Hazard) with a 3/35 14-day record — watch market moves between the pair as a pointer to which Palmer considers the better vehicle in these conditions.

races.name: Ebf Ashton In Makerfield Novice Stakes
Reprocolor Premier Ebf Fillies' Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Lady Roisia
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly has the clearest tactical advantage as the lone front runner; her one soft-ground win came over a shorter trip but she has performed respectably in similar conditions, and from OR 90 she sets the terms here — the 61-day absence is a minor query but Beckett handles returns well, and her style fit score reflects she is not being asked to deviate from her natural role.

runners_data.name: Miss Tonnerre
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's four-year-old has been off 99 days and has a deeply uninspiring recent form string with three finishes outside the top seven; she handles soft well enough on paper but zero wins or places from her last five runs in comparable company makes it hard to make a positive case despite the hold-up style that could theoretically suit a strong pace.

runners_data.name: Hoseki
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old has won three of her last five and is clearly in fine order; all those wins came on good or better ground, which is a genuine concern stepping into soft for the first time, and at OR 88 she is meeting some rivals on worse terms — Tom Marquand's positive style should see her travel prominently and she is the most likely horse to test Lady Roisia in the straight.

runners_data.name: Star Cast
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's mare has been in outstanding form on soft, winning twice and placing twice in her last four starts on that surface — the stats (5 soft runs, 2W 5P) are striking and she clearly thrives in these conditions; she will press up prominently from her natural position and the soft going is an unambiguous positive, though the trainer's 0-for-13 strike rate over 14 days is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Hollywell Stream
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up filly who won last time out on good ground over 10f; she has limited soft-ground exposure but showed promise when second in similar conditions over 7f, and Callum Shepherd will be looking to produce her late — she needs a genuine gallop to bring her into play in the straight.

runners_data.name: Polygram
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's four-year-old is a true hold-up or prominent-tracking type whose natural position has been displaced to midfield on the map because of the congested pace picture; she has won on soft and over this sort of trip, which is a genuine positive, but David Allan will need to be creative tactically and the style-fit discount is real — her recent form (342121) shows consistent competitiveness.

runners_data.name: Geo
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old is a natural prominent racer whose preferred berth is crowded out in this field; all five recent runs have come on good ground, which is an unambiguous going concern stepping into soft for the first time, and the combination of unfamiliar conditions and a redistributed map position makes her a difficult proposition — Lauren Young's claim may help the weights but not the tactical situation.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Roisia is the lone confirmed front runner and, with only Hoseki and Star Cast as genuine prominent types to challenge for early position, she is likely to stride into a clear lead and control tempo from the front at a pace she sets herself on soft ground. Hoseki and Star Cast will track up behind her, but neither is likely to apply genuine early pressure, meaning Lady Roisia can dictate a measured, energy-conserving gallop that suits stamina rather than finishing speed. Miss Tonnerre and Hollywell Stream will settle in the rear, with Polygram and Geo — both natural prominent or hold-up types crowded out of their preferred spots — mapped to midfield positions they would not naturally occupy; the field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural berths, and Lady Roisia and Hoseki are best placed to actually claim the positions that matter. This race shape strongly favours horses with the stamina to grind through soft ground from a prominent position, with Lady Roisia's front-running control the defining tactical factor, and those capable of tracking the leader into the straight without spending energy wide or in traffic holding the clearest edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Roisia sets an uncontested, measured tempo and holds enough in reserve to repel challengers from the straight.
scenarios.body: Lady Roisia controls every yard from the front, and the soft ground saps the finishing kick of hold-up horses before they can close; those who tracked prominently through the race have the best chance of pegging her back late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Roisia sets enough pace to tire herself and a horse tracking just off the leader produces a decisive move entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Hoseki or Star Cast, having sat a length or two off the front in a rhythm-saving position, picks up most cleanly when the leader weakens; the soft surface rewards the horse who does least early work while still travelling in touch.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely strong enough to bring hold-up horses into play and the soft ground stretches the field out over the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Hollywell Stream, a genuine hold-up filly with a soft-ground win on her card, would be the prime beneficiary if the pace burns up the prominent runners; Miss Tonnerre has the profile but her recent form is too cold to rely on.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Roisia sets a very slow early tempo and the race becomes a sprint finish off a crawl, nullifying the shape entirely.
scenarios.body: A dawdling pace on soft ground would compress the field and make running style irrelevant, handing an advantage to the horse with the sharpest finishing turn of foot — Polygram, a winner at this sort of trip, would be best-placed of the mid-pack types in that scenario, though its redistributed map position reflects that this is unlikely to materialise naturally.

watchPoints.text: Lady Roisia's front-running supremacy is the hinge of the whole race — if she breaks cleanly and is allowed to stride clear unchallenged, her ability to set her own pace on soft ground makes her very difficult to reel in over 1m2f.

Star Cast's soft-ground record (2W 5P from 5 starts) is the standout statistic in the field and means she must be respected as a prominent-tracking rival even if the trainer's recent 14-day strike rate is modest — she thrives precisely in today's conditions.

Hoseki has not raced on soft ground and all three wins came on good or good-to-firm; if the Haydock soft proves significantly more taxing than anything she has encountered, her ability to dominate from a prominent position could be compromised in the final furlong.

The midfield cluster of Polygram and Geo are both racing out of their most natural positions due to the compressed pace picture — neither should be assessed purely on map position, and both carry a meaningful style-fit discount that dampens their chance in this shape.

Miss Tonnerre's 99-day absence combined with three successive finishes outside the top seven makes it essential to see how she moves in the first half-mile; if she travels poorly or is immediately outpaced, her hold-up profile becomes irrelevant in a race unlikely to produce a truly hot gallop.

races.name: Visit Racingtv.com Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Sharp Move
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for Haggas and Marquand who returns on just six days' rest; soft ground is fine but her sole soft form sees her finish eighth in a 12f contest, and she needs competitors to tie each other up before she can land a blow from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Freddie Steady Go
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 5yo who produced his best when winning over 7f on soft for Susan Corbett; the jump to 1m2f is a significant step up in trip and an 82-day absence adds uncertainty, though soft ground is clearly his ally.

runners_data.name: Nightsinwhitesatin
runners_data.note: A model of consistency in defeat — five placings in five 12f starts on good ground for Edward Bethell — and the step into soft is the one unknown, but his prominent style and relentless galloping form make him a natural fit for this grind.

runners_data.name: Mehmas Champion
runners_data.note: Has drifted out of form badly across six starts, with a run on the all-weather doing little to arrest the slide; a hold-up horse by nature who will be shuffled further back than ideal in this large field, and a STYLE_FIT tag of 0.90 tempers enthusiasm for his chances here.

runners_data.name: High Point
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on soft and holds genuine course form; however, his natural hold-up style means he'll need the race to develop perfectly from deep, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 acknowledges he's likely to find himself out of his preferred rhythm in this shape.

runners_data.name: It'sneverjustone
runners_data.note: A prominent racer for Loughnane who has operated over shorter trips in recent starts; the move to 1m2f on soft tests his stamina, but his front-tracking instincts suit the predicted shape well and he deserves respect if getting this trip.

runners_data.name: Pearl Eye
runners_data.note: A genuinely hold-up horse who has been relocated to midfield on the map — in a field this large on soft, the 6yo Jim Goldie inmate will likely find herself further back than optimal, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 reflects the compromise to her race.

runners_data.name: Pomme Pomme
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner on a flat Haydock track in soft going; Clifford Lee can take this at face value and dictate, though a record of 0 wins from 2 soft-ground starts and a busy recent campaign (12 days since last run) temper expectations.

runners_data.name: Pol Roger
runners_data.note: Progressive and genuine for Michael Dods, winning over 10f on good and placing on soft; prominent style suits this shape, and the experience of Rhys Elliott guiding him from just off the pace makes him a consistent player in this scenario.

runners_data.name: Arcadian Nights
runners_data.note: An 8yo veteran who plugs on consistently without winning; prominent style is right for this race shape, but a form string of 45-465 and no win since his OR was higher indicate the handicapper has his measure.

runners_data.name: Knight Of Glory
runners_data.note: The David Menuisier 3yo has a win on soft and his hold-up style could work if the tempo is strong; he's been off 68 days and drops to a mark where his one-time Listed-level ability (1st at Sandown) may be overqualified for this grade.

runners_data.name: Blue To Blue
runners_data.note: Ruth Jefferson's 3yo has placed twice in five starts on good ground and carries genuine hold-up tendencies; shown at midfield on the map but naturally suited to racing off the pace, which the soft ground and large field may make even harder to exploit, STYLE_FIT 0.92.

runners_data.name: Night Patrol
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse for Camacho who won on soft over 7f and placed on soft over 8f; the step to 1m2f is a big ask and 90 days off the track adds risk, though his soft-ground form represents a genuine qualification in this going.

runners_data.name: Storm Point
runners_data.note: The Ed Walker 3yo has won on both soft and standard going and comes down in trip from 8f, but his prominent style is tailor-made for this race shape; T14 of 7/45 shows the stable is in decent form, and soft-ground experience adds significant appeal.

races.paceDynamic: Pomme Pomme is the lone confirmed front-runner in a field of 14 on soft ground at Haydock over 1m2f, and with no obvious challenger for the lead she is set to control proceedings from the front at a pace of her own choosing. Nightsinwhitesatin, It'sneverjustone, Pol Roger, Arcadian Nights, and Storm Point are genuine prominent types who will track Pomme Pomme through the early stages, creating a compact and organised head of the field rather than a chaotic battle for position. The soft ground will impose a relentless, grinding tempo even if the front end is not pressured, meaning the race will be run at an honest but sustainable pace that tests stamina throughout rather than producing a sudden late injection of speed. The dominant race shape favours horses who can travel prominently behind a lone leader and sustain their effort through the testing ground — prominent racers with stamina and form on soft going are most advantaged. Blue To Blue, Mehmas Champion, High Point, and Pearl Eye are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because the field is deeper in rear-runners than the visual positions suggest; of these, Mehmas Champion and Blue To Blue are most likely to actually secure a forward-of-midfield position given how crowded the true back of the field will be, but none of them will easily get their preferred position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Pomme Pomme sets a genuine but sustainable soft-ground tempo and the prominent trackers Nightsinwhitesatin, Pol Roger, and Storm Point travel comfortably in behind.
scenarios.body: The soft going rewards those who settle just off the pace and sustain their gallop through the final quarter-mile, with the hold-up brigade arriving too late on ground that kills acceleration.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Dictates, Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Pomme Pomme is allowed to set a falsely slow early tempo on the soft and builds an unassailable lead before the field wakes up.
scenarios.body: Clifford Lee can dictate every fraction, conserving energy through the testing ground, and a comfortable front-runner who has shown the ability to sustain effort could last home if the chasers leave it too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is strong enough to string the field out and the prominent types are worn down in the final two furlongs on the soft.
scenarios.body: Horses racing in the true midfield and hold-up positions — Knight Of Glory and Sharp Move with their proven soft-ground profiles — would have the energy reserves to pick off tiring rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos On Soft, Big Field
scenarios.trigger: If the 14-runner field causes crowding, interference, or significant scrimmaging throughout, disrupting the natural prominent types and flattening the pace.
scenarios.body: Horses that are handy enough to find clear runs but patient enough to avoid early scrimmaging would benefit, and a field this large on soft ground with tight weights compresses the finish.

watchPoints.text: Pomme Pomme is unchallenged for the lead — watch whether Clifford Lee elects to steal this on a soft-ground gallop or invites pursuit, as the outcome dictates every other runner's fate.

Nightsinwhitesatin has finished second in five consecutive races over 12f on good ground — the step onto soft today is the unknown quantity that could either unlock or undermine her consistent placed form.
Knight Of Glory returns after 68 days off and has the widest draw to manage in a 14-runner field; watch for any signs of rustiness or trouble finding a clear passage from the back third of the field.
